original_question: Given a weighted simple graph G = (V, E, omega) with geodesic distance d_G and a fixed epsilon > 0, what are the optimal upper and lower bounds on the cardinality of an epsilon-net L subseteq V for the metric space (V, d_G)? Here an epsilon-net means a landmark set that is both epsilon-sparse and an epsilon-sample of the graph.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Open Problem 1.1 in "The Dowker complex in metric graphs" (page 564 of the journal version): determine optimal upper and lower bounds for the number of elements of an ε-net for a weighted simple graph.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost verbatim. It has the correct ambient object (a weighted simple graph with induced geodesic distance), fixes ε>0, asks for optimal upper and lower bounds on the size of an ε-net, and correctly spells out that an ε-net is both ε-sparse and an ε-sample, exactly as in Definition 1.5.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone in the paper's sense, the graph should be taken as connected so that the induced geodesic distance d_G is a metric on V; the paper treats (V,d_G) as a finite metric space.
The weight function is specified in the background as ω:E→R_+.
It should be explicit that the quantity being bounded is |L| as L ranges over all ε-nets L⊂V for the fixed graph G and fixed ε, not the size of one preselected landmark set.
The ε-sample condition is formally stated using closed ε-neighborhoods: for every v∈V there exists u∈L with d_G(v,u)≤ε.

The motivating context immediately before the open problem is that an existing result already gives a nonsharp bound depending on ε, the diameter of G, and |V|; mentioning this helps anchor the question to the paper's exact intent.
refined_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a connected weighted simple graph with ω:E→R_+, and let d_G be the induced geodesic metric on the finite vertex set V. Fix ε>0. An ε-net for G is a subset L⊂V such that: (i) for every v∈V there exists u∈L with d_G(v,u)≤ε, and (ii) for all distinct u,u'∈L one has d_G(u,u')>ε. Determine the optimal upper and lower bounds on |L| over all ε-nets L of (V,d_G).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the extremal possible size of a landmark set L⊂V whose closed ε-neighborhoods cover V and whose pairwise d_G-distances are all strictly greater than ε.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Open Problem 1.1, not the neighboring problems. Open Problem 1.2 is algorithmic, asking for a faster/better ε-net construction method, and Open Problem 1.3 concerns persistence diagrams of Dowker versus Vietoris-Rips complexes. By contrast, your draft asks exactly for sharp upper and lower bounds on the cardinality of an ε-net. The only substantive refinements needed are to make explicit the connected finite-metric setting inherited from the background, the positivity of edge weights, and that the bounds are taken over all ε-nets L⊂V for the fixed graph and ε. The equivalent formulation is justified directly by Definition 1.5, which defines an ε-net as the conjunction of being an ε-sample and ε-sparse.
